metadata.title: Little Red Riding Hood
metadata.logline: On her way to Grandma's, Little Red Riding Hood trusts the Big Bad Wolf, and is saved by a hunter at the last moment.

char_red.motivation: to deliver cake and wine to her sick grandmother

char_wolf.name: Big Bad Wolf

scene_001.title: Mother's Warning
scene_001.summary: At home in the village, Little Red Riding Hood receives the basket her mother prepared and is told to take the main road and not talk to strangers.

char_mother.goal: warn her daughter to stay safe

beats.text: Little Red Riding Hood stands at the door, sunlight on her red cloak. Her mother comes out and hands her a wicker basket.
Mother, what's in the basket? It smells so good!
Her mother kneels to straighten the cloak and gently pats her cheek.
Her mother tells her: take the main road, do not linger in the woods, and do not talk to strangers.
Little Red Riding Hood nods hard, lifts the basket, and skips down the cobblestones toward the village gate.

scene_002.title: A Walk in the Woods
scene_002.summary: Little Red Riding Hood walks the sunny forest path, delighting in flowers and butterflies.

beats.text: Little Red Riding Hood walks the leaf-strewn trail, her red cloak flickering between shadows. She carries the basket in one hand and parts the bushes with the other.
A blue butterfly lands on the tip of her nose. She giggles and reaches for it, twirling among the flowers.
Grandma will love these flowers!
She bends to pick a few wildflowers and tucks them carefully into the basket. In the distant thicket, a pair of yellow eyes watches her.

scene_003.title: The Wolf Appears
scene_003.summary: In the deep forest the Big Bad Wolf stops Little Red Riding Hood, pretending to be friendly and coaxing out that she is going to Grandma's.
scene_003.mood: friendly on the surface, dangerous underneath

char_red.knowledge: thinks he is just a big dog

locationState.lighting: sunlight blocked, only stray beams through the canopy

beats.text: Little Red Riding Hood enters the deep forest and everything goes quiet. A tall figure steps slowly from behind the oak — a grey-brown Big Bad Wolf.
Hello there, little girl. Where are you going?
Little Red Riding Hood is not afraid. She does not know the wolf and thinks he looks like a big dog.
I'm going to Grandma's to bring her cake and wine. She's sick, and lives in the cottage on the other side of the woods.
The wolf's ears prick up and his tail gives a twitch. In his mind he is already scheming.
There are so many lovely flowers in these woods. Why not pick some to bring to Grandma?
Little Red Riding Hood looks at the flowers by the path, eyes brightening. As she turns to pick them, the wolf slips silently away into the thicket.

scene_004.title: The Wolf's Trick
scene_004.summary: The Big Bad Wolf races a shortcut to Grandma's, knocks and deceives her, then swallows her whole.

beats.text: The wolf runs panting to Grandma's door. He smooths his fur and lowers his voice.
Grandma, it's me, Little Red Riding Hood. I've brought you cake.
Just lift the latch, child. Grandma is too tired to get up today.
The wolf pushes the door open and bares his white teeth. Grandma's eyes widen in terror, but she cannot call for help.

scene_005.title: The Disguise
scene_005.summary: The Big Bad Wolf puts on Grandma's nightgown and cap, and lies in bed waiting for Little Red Riding Hood.

char_wolf.appearance: wearing Grandma's white nightgown and lace cap, bundled under the covers

locationState.lighting: firelight throws shadows on the wall, dim
locationState.condition: bedding rumpled, signs of a struggle on the floor

beats.text: The wolf clumsily pulls on Grandma's white nightgown and jams the lace cap onto his head, pointed ears poking out at the edges.
He climbs into bed and pulls the covers to his chin, leaving only the capped head showing. The firelight makes it look almost seamless.
Light footsteps and a little girl's humming drift in from outside. The wolf grins.

scene_006.title: The Classic Questions
scene_006.summary: Little Red Riding Hood arrives and questions the wolf's eyes, ears and mouth, until he reveals his true face.
scene_006.mood: suspense rising from doubt to terror

char_wolf.appearance: sheds the Grandma disguise, throwing off the covers to reveal grey-brown fur and sharp teeth

prop_basket.appearance: set on the table, checkered cloth folded back

beats.text: Little Red Riding Hood pushes the door open and sets the basket on the table. She walks to the bed and thinks Grandma looks different today.
Grandma, what big ears you have!

beats.tone: muffling his voice to mimic Grandma
beats.text: The better to hear you with, my child.
Grandma, what big eyes you have!
The better to see you with, my child.
Grandma, what a big mouth you have!
The better to EAT you with!
The wolf throws off the covers and lunges at Little Red Riding Hood. She screams.

scene_007.title: The Hunter Arrives
scene_007.summary: A passing hunter hears strange snoring inside, breaks in and finds the wolf.

char_wolf.appearance: belly swollen, still in Grandma's nightgown, snoring in bed

locationState.lighting: afternoon sun slanting through the window
locationState.condition: room in disarray, bedding askew, Grandma's slippers scattered on the floor

beats.text: The hunter passes the cottage on his rounds and hears thunderous snoring. He frowns — the old woman could never snore like that.
Something's wrong...
The hunter eases the door open and sees a big-bellied wolf in Grandma's nightgown, snoring on the bed.
The hunter swings the axe off his back and steps toward the bed. He notices the wolf's swollen belly is still moving.

scene_008.title: Reunion
scene_008.summary: The hunter frees Grandma and Little Red Riding Hood with his axe; the three are reunited and she learns her lesson.

locationState.lighting: sunlight through the window, warm and bright
locationState.condition: the cottage tidy and cozy again, fire dancing in the hearth

prop_basket.appearance: opened, cake and wine set on the table

prop_axe.appearance: resting against the wall in a corner

beats.text: The hunter carefully cuts open the wolf's belly with his axe. Little Red Riding Hood jumps out first, then Grandma is freed.
Grandma!
Little Red Riding Hood hugs Grandma tightly as she weakly strokes her hair. The hunter stands aside with a relieved smile.
The three sit around the table eating cake from the basket. Sunlight pours through the window; all is calm again.
From that day on, Little Red Riding Hood never disobeyed her mother again. She had learned the most important lesson: do not trust a stranger's sweet words.

acts.title: Act I: Setting Out
acts.summary: At her mother's bidding, Little Red Riding Hood carries the basket toward Grandma's and meets the Big Bad Wolf in the forest.

acts.title: Act II: The Crisis
acts.summary: The wolf reaches Grandma's first, swallows her, and disguises himself to wait for Little Red Riding Hood.

acts.title: Act III: The Rescue
acts.summary: The hunter arrives in time, frees Little Red Riding Hood and Grandma, and the wolf is punished.

thread_main.name: Main Plot
thread_main.description: Little Red Riding Hood delivers food and meets the Big Bad Wolf.

logicRelations.description: The yellow eyes in the thicket foreshadow the meeting in the woods.
Little Red Riding Hood reveals Grandma's address, prompting the wolf to race there.
The hunter frees Little Red Riding Hood and Grandma, leading to the reunion.

characterRelations.description: Little Red Riding Hood does not know the wolf.
